intro.title: Specialist IT translation for hardware, software and telecoms
paras: IT translations must be accurate, and there is no room for doubt. English is everywhere in the sector, so only a specialist knows which terms to translate and which to leave in English.
For businesses that also need the software itself designed or localised, we work alongside development partners such as Globaprom.
checks: Translators with prior professional experience in information and communications technology
The same translators allocated to the same client, so terminology stays consistent
Version control that keeps content and style consistent across updates
Dutch, French, Spanish, German and Asian languages such as Korean

services.title: IT translation services we carry out regularly
services.lead: A few examples of the work our clients ask for most often.

items.title: User interfaces
items.text: UX and UI text, and requests from users to programmers.

items.title: Test scenarios
items.text: User acceptance (UAT) and compliance (ITT) test scenarios.

items.title: Online games
items.text: Game text translated for each player market.

items.title: Software and hardware documents
items.text: User and installation manuals, intranet and extranet content, training kits and telecoms FAQs.

items.title: Tenders and bids
items.text: Calls for bids and tender specifications for IT and telecommunications contracts.

items.title: Cloud and security
items.text: Applications and manuals for cloud computing and security software such as VPN, firewall and antivirus.

items.title: Dedicated project managers
items.text: Each document is often the basis for several future versions, so we plan for them.

items.title: Software localisation
items.text: Not everything needs re-localising with each update, which keeps costs sensible for regular clients.

items.title: Consistent terminology
items.text: The same specialist translators work on your projects from one job to the next.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
items: Which IT documents can you translate?
We translate software strings, interfaces, user guides, technical documentation, data sheets and training documents.
Tell us what you have and we confirm the best fit.
Do you translate terms or leave them in English?
Our IT specialists decide which terms to translate and which to keep in English.
They follow the conventions of your sector and language.
We translate software strings and related documentation.
Where the software itself must be designed or localised, we work alongside development partners.
How do you keep terminology consistent?
We allocate the same translators to the same client.
Version control keeps content and style consistent across updates.
